narrative:
The model determined that you have a 29% chance of representing a bad credit risk. While this is not a majority prediction, the bank’s threshold for approval requires stronger confidence that the loan will be repaid, so your application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outcome were the status of your checking account, your other installment plans, and the length of the loan you requested. Your checking account status had the largest impact and worked in your favor: having no checking account is actually the most common situation among approved applicants (59%). This gave the model a meaningful reason to view you more positively.

However, the presence of an existing installment plan with a bank pushed the prediction noticeably toward bad credit risk. This signal suggested higher existing financial commitments that could make repayment harder. The shorter 12-month duration you requested worked in your favor compared to the 19-month average among approved loans, but this positive effect was not large enough to overcome the concern created by your other installment plan.

Taken together, these factors left the model insufficiently confident in your application. To improve your chances next time, focus on paying down or closing any existing installment agreements before reapplying, and consider requesting a slightly longer repayment period if your budget allows. This would remove the strongest negative signal the model saw.
